CAUSE: `NO_COMMITS_MERGED` is a generic label that hides the real failure. The code overwrites the specific error, so I can't name the exact failure from the code alone. It is most likely a dirty `main` checkout or a merge conflict, and I haven't confirmed which.

Evidence:
- `merge_worktree_to_main` in `app/workspace.py` reads `target_before` early (around line 1337). From that point on, every failure it returns has no `commits_merged` key and leaves `main` unmoved.
- Those failures include:
  - a dirty target checkout: `_clean_worktree_error(target_wt, "target")`, line 1429;
  - the `merge-tree` conflict precheck, around lines 1497-1520;
  - `prepare` journal failures, `git merge --squash` failures, and `TARGET_HEAD_CHANGED`;
  - the check at line 1347 that the worker HEAD already equals the target.
- Each of these carries its own specific error text, such as "target working tree is dirty (N file(s): …)" or a list of conflict paths.
- `normalize_merge_result` in `app/merge_operations.py` (lines 1020-1036) treats any result as "no commits merged" when `target_before == target_after` and `int(commits_merged or 0) == 0`. The check doesn't test `ok`. It then replaces `ok`, `state`, `code` and `error` with `NO_COMMITS_MERGED` and "merge produced no new commits".
- The real error text and code are lost at that point. The same is true of any `TARGET_HEAD_CHANGED` result, because the rewrite runs before `_classify_failure` is called. The route in `app/routes/sessions.py:2102-2115` does a similar rewrite, but only when `ok` is true.
- That is why repeating the call gives the same answer. The normalizer produces the same label every time, whatever the underlying failure is.
- The `next_action` text, "verify the worker branch", points at the wrong place. The worker branch is fine, since `git log main..task-416/worker` shows the commit.

I could not look at the live repository. This snapshot has no git data, and I was told not to touch the live service.

Recommended fix:
1. Diagnose now. Run `git status --porcelain` in the main checkout that holds `main`. Untracked files count as dirty there, so any stray or untracked file blocks the merge. Also run `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main task-416/worker` to check for conflicts. Then clean or commit the main checkout, or resolve the conflict on the worker branch, and start a new merge operation.
2. Fix the code in `app/merge_operations.py`.
   - Apply the `no_commits_merged` rewrite only when `raw.get("ok")` is true and `raw.get("code")` is unset, as `app/routes/sessions.py` already does. Never override a result that already has an `error`, `code` or `conflicts`.
   - Keep the original `error` in `details`, for example as `upstream_error`.
   - Then `_classify_failure` can return `TARGET_DIRTY`, `CONFLICT` or `TARGET_HEAD_CHANGED` with the right `next_action`.
